body: Suikoden II is Konami's PlayStation role-playing game, first released in Japan on 17 December 1998. Three years after the original, war between Highland and the City-States of Jowston draws a young soldier and his friend Jowy into opposing responsibilities. Each receives half of the Rune of the Beginning, tying their personal relationship to a larger conflict. Yoshitaka Murayama directed the adventure, with music by Miki Higashino and Keiko Fukami. Recruiting the 108 Stars of Destiny makes the growing resistance a community of people, rather than a party that exists only for the next battle.

The player finds allies through conversations, exploration and small tasks, bringing more than a hundred possible recruits to the cause. Only some fight in the ordinary party; others give the base additional activities and services. The organisation therefore becomes visible through the people who live there. Towns also offer equipment, weapon sharpening and runes, while the surrounding country brings random encounters. Lower-level companions gain experience quickly against stronger enemies, helping newly recruited characters catch up. Choosing a different party becomes practical without requiring every newcomer to repeat the same long training route.

Ordinary party battles share the adventure with individual duels and larger clashes between armies. Each format gives the conflict a different scale, moving from a personal confrontation to the forces gathered around the protagonist. Runes provide magic and specialised abilities, with limited spell uses asking for planning across encounters. Save data from the first game can alter references and strengthen returning characters, connecting this new war to an earlier journey. Later compilations and the 2025 HD remaster brought the original pair to further hardware.
